text_blocks.snippet: A diet for gastroenteritis, also known as the stomach flu, should focus on rehydration and easily digestible foods to help the body recover. Avoid fatty, spicy, and sugary foods, as well as caffeine, alcohol, and dairy, which can worsen symptoms. Focus on bland, low-fiber foods that are easy on the stomach, and gradually reintroduce regular foods as tolerated.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rehydration and easily digestible foods to help the body recover

list.title: Hydration is key:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of fluids like water, clear broth, or oral rehydration solutions to replace lost fluids and electrolytes. Avoid sugary drinks like apple juice, which can worsen diarrhea.
Crackers, toast, and rice: These are low in fiber and easy to digest.
Bananas, applesauce: These are good sources of potassium and can help with diarrhea.
Chicken or fish (plain): Choose lean, cooked proteins with minimal seasoning.
Plain noodles, mashed potatoes: These are low in fiber and easy to digest.
Gelatin: A simple and bland option for hydration.

list.title: Low-fat dairy products:
list.snippet: Yogurt and low-fat milk can be soothing for some, but avoid if they cause discomfort.

list.title: Eggs:
list.snippet: A good source of protein and energy.

list.title: Fruits and cooked vegetables:
list.snippet: When you can tolerate them, introduce fresh fruits (avoiding citrus) and cooked vegetables.
High-fat foods: Fried foods, fatty meats, and rich sauces can be difficult to digest.
Spicy foods: These can irritate the stomach and worsen diarrhea.
Sugary foods and drinks: Sodas, candy, and ice cream can exacerbate diarrhea.
Caffeine and alcohol: These can dehydrate the body and irritate the stomach.
Dairy (in some cases): Some people find dairy products worsen diarrhea, so it's best to avoid them initially.
Fibre-rich foods: Initially, avoid foods high in fiber, like beans, lentils, and some fruits and vegetables, as they can increase stool frequency.
Eat small, frequent meals: This can be easier on the stomach than large meals.
Listen to your body: Stop eating if you experience nausea or vomiting.
Get plenty of rest: Rest allows your body to recover.
Consult a doctor if symptoms are severe or persistent: If you have severe dehydration, high fever, or bloody stools, seek medical attention.
